title: Recovery of compatible original levels from a torsion-controlled second-ideal triple
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideals, $M\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,I)$, and $H$ coherent, as in [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Suppose $\alpha:M\to\widehat H_I$ has component kernels and cokernels killed by one positive power of $K$. Let $N\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,K)$, $\delta:N\to\widehat H_K$, and an isomorphism of double diagrams $\sigma_{e,n}:N_e/I^nN_e\simeq M_n/K^eM_n$ be given. Let $\theta_{e,n}:(H/K^eH)/I^n\simeq(H/I^nH)/K^e$ be the quotient interchange characterized by the projections from $H$, and assume the comparison square with $\alpha_n$ and $\delta_e$ commutes. Let $F$ be coherent, $a:F\to H$ have actual kernel and cokernel killed by one positive power of $K$, and $\beta:N\simeq\widehat F_K$ satisfy $\delta=\widehat a_K\circ\beta$. Then there exist isomorphisms $\varphi_n:F/I^nF\simeq M_n$ for all positive $n$, compatible with every transition of the I-adic diagrams.

proof.text: For each positive n, evaluate the doubly indexed comparison in the I-index. Reduce beta modulo I^n and commute the two quotients using their cokernel universal properties. The projection equation for theta and the square identify the completed map with the K-completion of alpha_n.

Remark 0888 bounds the kernel and cokernel of a modulo I^n by K^(2s). Thus F/I^n F with its reduced map and M_n with alpha_n are torsion-controlled triples for the same K-completed map. The torsion-controlled uniqueness statement gives a canonical isomorphism between their coherent sources.

For a transition, the two composites agree after K-completion by the naturality of sigma and beta. Away from V(K), the torsion-controlled comparison maps to the corresponding quotient of H are invertible, so the composites agree there as well. On an affine open, injectivity in the formal gluing complex makes maps agreeing on the completion and those localizations equal. Local equality then gives global equality, proving transition compatibility.
